# laravelcloud_environment_variable (Resource)

Manages one environment variable of an environment in Laravel Cloud.

Each resource manages a single key and leaves the environment's other variables alone, so variables set in the dashboard or with the `cloud` CLI can live next to the ones Terraform manages.

A new or changed value is stored right away but only reaches the application with the next deployment: Laravel Cloud does not redeploy the environment when a variable changes ([docs](https://cloud.laravel.com/docs/environments)), so deploy the environment afterwards.

Creating a variable whose key is already set on the environment fails instead of overwriting it; import the variable to manage it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "website_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "laravelcloud_environment_variable" "website_token" {
  environment = "environment-id"
  key         = "CRM_WEBSITE_TOKEN"
  value       = var.website_token
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment` (String) The identifier of the environment the variable belongs to.
- `key` (String) The name of the variable, such as `APP_KEY`: a letter or underscore followed by letters, digits and underscores.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The value of the variable.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import laravelcloud_environment_variable.example environment-id/CRM_WEBSITE_TOKEN
```
